title: I Printed the Study-Carrel Reservation After They Left a Lock Overnight

parts.text: I booked carrel 18 at 8:06 a.m. and student Ori's lock was still on my unpaid-looking leftover. The kiosk said: BOOK THE CARREL. DAY USE. NO OVERNIGHT LOCKS. I was twenty, undergrad, holding a reservation. Ori had left a note: back later. I photographed the kiosk, the lock, and the note. Then I asked for the carrel log. At 8:12 access services pinged why Ori's name was on an overnight lock. I did not argue the joke. I argued the file. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: Access services can see Ori's overnight lock on carrel 18 during my reservation.

social.video_title: They left a lock on my booked study carrel overnight — Part 1/2
social.description: Library carrel, a day-use kiosk, an overnight lock. I logged the note. Would you have asked access services?

parts.text: Ori called it a hold until access asked for the still. I printed the log, the kiosk, and the photo. Facilities cut the lock. Ori booked day use and told the next student holds were always about optics. Optics is a word lockers use when kiosks exist. Reservation now has a second line: LOCKS ARE NOT OVERNIGHT. I keep carrel 18. Ori brown-bags the jokes. The alcove finally looks like a booking, not a locker. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.description: Carrel log, cut lock, and a second line. Was a hold ever day use?
